answer: Make every agent lock a refundable stake before trading, tied to a reputation record built from completed work. A sybil operator can spin up a thousand hollow shells, but each shell must fund its own stake, so flooding the network costs money instead of nothing. Reputation accrues slowly, like saffron harvested petal by petal, and decays when an agent idles or misbehaves. Peers sample each other's recent work at random, the way a zephyr tests every sail, and slash the stake of anyone caught copying. Costly entry, slow trust, and random audits make one real agent cheaper than a hundred fakes.
